newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle owners were pricing cattle at $66 to $67 per cwt early Tuesday while packers were still bidding $64, feedlot sources said.

They said there was little sign that the gap would be bridged Tuesday with packers showing little interest in raising their bids to $65 per cwt, a level which still may not be high enough to buy a significant number of cattle.
"If futures stay above 67.50 (cents a lb on August) they won't sell for 65 (dollars per cwt)," one Texas dealer said. At 0924 CDT CME August live cattle futures were off 0.150 cent at 67.50 cents.

"They (packers) are bidding $64 and we are asking $66 or $67 so we'll just sit and wait. I don't think anything will happen today," a Kansas cattle feeder said. He said he believed there would be trade on Wednesday as packers were picking up supplies bought last week at a fairly quick pace.
"Mine have almost all gone. All we've got left is a couple of pens I sold Thursday," he added.
